summary:
All four ratings are locked in on 14 of 15 games today, and that kind of unanimous consensus is exactly when the trends category matters most — trends is running hot across the board at 108-80 (57%, n=188) for R1, R2 and R3 alike, and it's also the anchor of the top category combo, trends+runs at 56.7% (n=436). That combo lines up cleanly with the CIN@ARI game, the day's biggest delta (R4 ARI +3.08, all four models north of +2.8), and with MIL, a team that rewards the model handsomely when picked (27-15, 64%, strong plays 16-8 for +6.0u) — ATL@MIL is another full-consensus lean in the +2.0 to +2.3 range across all raters. BOS also shows up on today's board (SFG@BOS) sitting in a spot where the model has hit 30-9 (77%) on the season and 16-5 (+15.0u) on strong plays, making it a green light even though the delta there (+1.0 to +1.7) is more modest than the top-tier games.

Where to be careful: R2's runs category is ice cold right now, -5.6pts off baseline at 47% (89-99, n=188), so any thin edge driven mainly by runs disagreement should get discounted — watch LAA@TEX, the only split board today, where R2 breaks off to like LAA while R1/R3/R4 lean TEX; that's a low-confidence spot best skipped or minimally staked. Bullpen is the steadiest recent category across R1-R3, all sitting at 55% (104-84, n=188), which supports playing through the CLE@COL fade (all four books hate CLE, -1.5 to -1.7) and the LAD lean over PIT, where LAD's strong-play track record is elite (14-2, 88%, +17.0u). R4 is small-sample but scorching (79% on trends, 19-5) — treat it as confirmation on the consensus plays rather than a standalone signal given n=24. Overall, stack today's bets around ARI, MIL, and BOS where trend/runs agreement and hot team histories intersect, and go light on games driven by runs-category separation given R2's current cold streak.
